drills.title: Read the Hazard
drills.description: Placards, diamonds, the ERG, and PPE. Ten seconds each — you're reading through binoculars.

items.prompt: You know the 4-digit UN number. Which ERG pages?
items.why: Yellow pages are sorted by ID number.

items.prompt: You need the initial isolation distance for a toxic gas.
items.why: Green pages = isolation and protective action distances.

items.prompt: NFPA diamond: the BLUE quadrant shows 4.
items.why: Blue = health; 4 = can be lethal with short exposure.

items.prompt: NFPA white quadrant shows 'W' with a line through it.
Unknown vapor, entry team going into the hot zone.
items.why: Unknown vapor hazards require maximum skin + respiratory protection.

items.prompt: Hospital decon team, agent known, oxygen normal.
items.why: Level C (APR/PAPR + splash suit) is typical for hospital/decon teams with known agents.

items.prompt: Five people collapsed in a basement, no trauma, rotten-egg smell.
options: Do not approach — withdraw, report, request HazMat (Step 3)
items.why: 3+ casualties unexplained = Step 3. Rotten egg suggests hydrogen sulfide — smell fades as it paralyzes olfaction.

items.prompt: First and best decon step for 100 exposed people?
items.why: Disrobing removes most external contamination immediately.

items.prompt: Exposure to a vapor only, patients asymptomatic, no visible liquid.
items.why: Dry decon is the default for most exposures; wet for caustics/liquid/symptoms.
